newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open down in line with Dow.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open down in line with Dow.

text.p: Australian shares drifted lower from the open on Thursday, the market reacting predictably to a weaker Wall Street and a further fall of base metals on the London Metal Exchange.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.1 points lower at 2,300.6.
The December share price index was six points down at 2,326 and at a 25.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said stocks opened lower across the board and most blue chip issues started lower, except food and beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil.

"The pattern of the market in the last few days has been a sharp sell-off at the open followed by a modest recovery then another sell-off. It has started this way again," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said a stable local bond market was lending the market some support to equities and the fact that the Japanese equity market was closed for a holiday meant there was one less factor to worry Australian investors.
The release of September labour force data later this morning could be a significant factor for the market if the figures were well above or below analysts forecasts, dealers said.
Dealers said a large number of issues were ex-dividend and this would have a slight negative effect on the level of the All Ordinaries index throughout the session.
